record.paper_title: Selection Principles and Special Sets of Reals
record.original_question: For a topological group G, let Onbd denote the covers {g·U : g ∈ G} arising from neighborhoods U of the identity. Are there, in ZFC, groups G and H that satisfy Sfin(Onbd, O) even though G × H does not?

evidence.quote: Are there, in ZFC, groups G, H satisfying Sfin(Onbd, O) such that G × H does not satisfy Sfin(Onbd, O)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a topological group with identity $e$. For each neighborhood $U$ of $e$, let $\mathcal{C}_U = \{gU : g \in G\}$ be the cover of $G$ by left translates of $U$, and let $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{nbd}}(G) = \{\mathcal{C}_U : U \text{ a neighborhood of } e\}$. Let $\mathcal{O}(G)$ denote the family of all open covers of $G$.

Recall Scheepers' selection principle $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{B})$: for every sequence $(\mathcal{U}_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ with each $\mathcal{U}_n \in \mathcal{A}$, there exist finite subfamilies $\mathcal{F}_n \subseteq \mathcal{U}_n$ such that $\bigcup_{n \in \mathbb{N}} \mathcal{F}_n \in \mathcal{B}$.

A topological group $G$ is said to satisfy $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{nbd}}, \mathcal{O})$ if, for every sequence $(U_n)_{n \in \mathbb{N}}$ of neighborhoods of $e$, there exist finite subsets $F_n \subseteq G$ such that $\{f U_n : n \in \mathbb{N},\ f \in F_n\}$ is an open cover of $G$.

Question: Does there exist, provably in ZFC, a pair of topological groups $G$ and $H$ such that both $G$ and $H$ satisfy $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{nbd}}, \mathcal{O})$, while the product group $G \times H$ does not?
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not surface a definitive ZFC construction or a proof of impossibility of the described product pathology for the property $S_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{nbd}}, \mathcal{O})$. Related work on o-bounded groups and Menger-type selection principles (e.g., Tsaban's work and consistency results in the Miller model) addresses neighboring questions but does not appear to resolve this one in ZFC. Status is therefore reported as unknown.

status_evidence.title: o-Bounded Groups and Other Topological Groups with Strong Combinatorial Properties
status_evidence.snippet: Study of o-bounded groups and related selection-principle properties in topological groups.
status_evidence.claim: Provides background and related results on o-bounded groups but does not settle the stated ZFC product question.

status_evidence.title: Countable dense homogeneous filters and the Menger covering property
status_evidence.snippet: Menger property is preserved by finite products of metrizable spaces in the Miller model; in ZFC the situation is more delicate.
status_evidence.claim: Indicates that product behavior of Menger-type properties is sensitive to set-theoretic assumptions, supporting an unknown ZFC status.
